subject: history_social
passage: Until the 1890s, many farm families in the United States had to travel to a post office in town to collect their mail. In 1896, the government began delivering mail directly to some rural homes. Historian Ruth Adler argues that this new service caused a rise in the number of farm families who subscribed to daily newspapers.
stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken Adler's argument?

choices.A: Many farm families also used the delivery service to receive catalogs and letters from relatives.
choices.B: Subscriptions rose just as fast among farm families who still collected their mail in town.
choices.C: Daily newspapers of the 1890s often printed crop prices and weather reports that were useful to farmers.
choices.D: Subscriptions rose sharply in rural areas soon after home delivery of mail reached them.

explanation.why: Adler says home mail delivery caused more farm families to subscribe to newspapers. If families without home delivery increased their subscriptions just as fast, delivery cannot be the cause.
explanation.A: Incorrect. What else families received by mail does not show whether delivery increased newspaper subscriptions.
explanation.B: Correct. Families without home delivery subscribed at the same growing rate, so the delivery service does not explain the rise.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This gives a reason farmers might want newspapers, but it does not test whether home delivery caused the rise.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Subscriptions jumping right after delivery began would support Adler's argument, not weaken it.
